description: Reflection Dashboard page — evaluates the effectiveness of AI self-healing fixes across workflow executions, providing aggregated metrics, run history, and individual fix analysis.

groups.name: Effectiveness Overview and Metrics
groups.description: The Reflection Dashboard provides users with a high-level view of how well the AI's self-healing capabilities are performing. Users need to see aggregate statistics including the total number of fixes applied, how many were effective vs ineffective, whether any caused regressions, and the overall effectiveness rate as a percentage. These summary cards give users confidence (or concern) about the reliability of the reflection system, helping them decide whether to continue relying on automated fixes or intervene with manual corrections. The data should be scoped to a specific workflow, since effectiveness patterns vary significantly between different automation tasks.

assertions.description: Users can identify the Reflection Effectiveness dashboard and understand its purpose as a tool for evaluating how well AI self-healing fixes are performing across workflow executions
Users can see the total number of fixes that the reflection system has applied, providing a measure of how actively the self-healing system is working
Users can see the count of fixes that were determined to be effective, giving them confidence in the proportion of self-healing attempts that actually improved workflow outcomes
Users can see the overall effectiveness rate as a percentage, providing a single metric that summarizes how reliably the reflection system produces beneficial fixes

groups.name: Workflow-Scoped Analysis
groups.description: Since reflection effectiveness varies greatly between workflows, users need to scope their analysis to a specific workflow. The dashboard should provide a workflow selector populated with names from recent task runs, and automatically load data for the selected workflow. Users should be able to switch between workflows to compare effectiveness patterns and identify which automations benefit most from self-healing. When no reflection data exists for a selected workflow, a clear message should explain that fixes will appear after workflow executions occur.

assertions.description: Users can select a specific workflow from a dropdown to scope the reflection analysis, allowing them to evaluate self-healing effectiveness for each workflow independently

When no reflection fixes exist for the selected workflow, users see an informative empty state explaining that reflection data will appear after workflow executions, rather than a confusing blank dashboard
Users can manually refresh the reflection data to pick up newly completed workflow runs without navigating away from the dashboard

groups.name: Reflection Run History
groups.description: Beyond aggregate metrics, users need to see the timeline of individual reflection runs. The history section shows recent reflection executions with their task run IDs, completion status (complete, running, failed), fix counts, and timestamps. This chronological view helps users understand the cadence of self-healing activity, identify runs that produced many fixes (potentially indicating systemic issues), and correlate reflection outcomes with specific workflow execution attempts.

assertions.description: Users can see a list of recent reflection runs showing when each self-healing cycle occurred, how many fixes it produced, and whether it completed successfully
Each reflection run entry shows its completion status with color-coded badges so users can quickly distinguish successful, in-progress, and failed self-healing cycles

groups.name: Individual Fix Analysis
groups.description: For deeper investigation, users need to drill into individual fixes to understand exactly what the reflection system changed. Each fix entry shows the fix type (knowledge update, step rewrite, selector fix, tool config, context addition, instruction clarification), a description, confidence level, and effectiveness assessment. Expanding a fix reveals the file changed, old and new values, application timestamp, and effectiveness evidence. This level of detail is essential for users who want to audit the AI's self-healing decisions, validate that fixes are appropriate, or learn from the patterns of successful vs unsuccessful corrections.

assertions.description: Users can see a list of all individual fixes with their types, descriptions, confidence levels, and effectiveness assessments, enabling granular review of what the reflection system has changed

Users can expand individual fixes to see detailed before/after values, the specific file changed, and evidence supporting the effectiveness assessment, providing full auditability of AI self-healing decisions

target.label: Expanded fix detail with old/new values

assertions.description: Each fix displays its type category (Knowledge Update, Step Rewrite, Selector Fix, etc.) so users can identify patterns in what kinds of corrections the AI applies most frequently

states.name: Loading State
states.description: Initial loading state while fetching workflow list and reflection data from the backend. A spinner is visible and no report content is rendered yet.

transitions.name: Load completes with no data
transitions.description: Fetched data returns no reflection fixes for the selected workflow, showing the empty state

transitions.name: Load completes with data
transitions.description: Fetched data returns reflection fixes, showing summary cards, run history, and fix list

states.name: Empty State — No Fixes
states.description: No reflection fixes exist for the selected workflow. An informational message is displayed explaining that reflection data will appear after workflow executions.

transitions.name: Select a different workflow
transitions.description: Change the workflow selector to load data for a different workflow, returning to the loading state

transitions.name: Refresh data
transitions.description: Click the refresh button to re-fetch reflection data for the current workflow

states.name: Data Loaded — Dashboard View
states.description: Reflection data is loaded and displayed. Summary metric cards (Total Fixes, Effective, Ineffective, Effectiveness Rate) are visible along with recent reflection runs, trend charts (when available), the full fix list with all fixes collapsed, and the Graph Insights sub-tab section.

transitions.name: Expand a fix
transitions.description: Click on a fix row to expand it and reveal detailed before/after values, file changed, and effectiveness evidence

transitions.name: Select a different workflow
transitions.description: Change the workflow selector to load data for a different workflow

transitions.name: Refresh data
transitions.description: Click the refresh button to re-fetch reflection data

transitions.name: Switch Graph Insights tab
transitions.description: Click a Graph Insights sub-tab (Cross-Run Patterns, Rule Influence, Pipeline Events, Step Provenance, Versions) to change the displayed insight panel

states.name: Fix Detail Expanded
states.description: One or more fix rows are expanded, revealing detailed information including the file changed, application status, timestamp, old and new values, reasoning, alternatives considered, and effectiveness evidence.

transitions.name: Collapse fix detail
transitions.description: Click the expanded fix row again to collapse it and return to the dashboard view

transitions.name: Expand another fix
transitions.description: Click a different fix row to expand it while keeping the current one expanded

transitions.name: Select a different workflow
transitions.description: Change workflow selector to load data for a different workflow, collapsing all fixes

transitions.name: Refresh data
transitions.description: Click the refresh button to re-fetch data, collapsing all expanded fixes
